mainEntity.name: How much does a Toyota RAV4 2.5 PHEV engine replacement cost in the UK?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Toyota RAV4 2.5 PHEV A25A-FXS engine replacement typically costs £1,472-£2,400 for a used unit, £2,500-£4,200 for a reconditioned engine, and £3,800-£5,500 for a fully rebuilt unit (supply only). Fitting adds approximately £1,200-£1,800 in labour (10-14 hours at specialist rates).

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of A25A-FXS engine failure in a Toyota RAV4 2.5 PHEV?

acceptedAnswer.text: Common warning signs include the 'Maintenance Required' or 'Check Engine' light (coolant bypass valve failure with codes P261B or P261C), hybrid system malfunction errors (high-voltage cable corrosion), loss of cabin heat, overheating, and unusual engine noise.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Toyota RAV4 2.5 PHEV?

acceptedAnswer.text: For a Toyota RAV4 2.5 PHEV worth £28,000-£45,000, a rebuilt A25A-FXS engine (£3,800-£5,500 supply) is almost always a sound investment. The RAV4 2.5 PHEV retains strong value, and a quality rebuilt unit with warranty offers better long-term value than scrapping the car.

mainEntity.name: How long does a Toyota RAV4 2.5 PHEV engine replacement take?

acceptedAnswer.text: A Toyota RAV4 2.5 PHEV A25A-FXS engine replacement typically takes 10-14 hours for a specialist workshop. Supply-only delivery takes 1-2 days, and supply & fit typically requires 2-4 working days total, depending on workshop availability.

mainEntity.name: Is the Toyota RAV4 2.5 PHEV A25A-FXS engine reliable?

acceptedAnswer.text: The A25A-FXS is generally reliable, but several issues have been documented. The coolant bypass valve can seize (60,000-100,000 miles), the high-voltage cable can corrode ('Cablegate'), and EGR cooler leaks have been reported. Toyota also issued a recall for potential engine cracks in some 2019-2020 models.

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between the RAV4 2.5 PHEV and the standard RAV4 Hybrid engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: The RAV4 2.5 PHEV uses the same A25A-FXS 2.5-litre Atkinson-cycle petrol engine as the standard hybrid, but with a larger 18.1kWh lithium-ion battery and more powerful electric motors, delivering 302bhp (38% more than the standard hybrid) and a 46-mile EV range.

While generally reliable, the complexity of the plug-in hybrid system introduces specific failure points that owners should be aware of. Rebuilt engines through EnginesMarket include upgraded components addressing the original failure points, plus a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

problems.h4: Coolant Bypass Valve Failure - Why the Toyota RAV4 2.5 PHEV A25A-FXS Suffers Thermal Management Issues
problems.rootCause: The engine coolant bypass valve assembly manages engine thermal stratification by routing coolant through the heater core and engine blocks. Over time, the internal polymer valve seals degrade or the electrical actuator motor seizes, causing the valve to stick closed. This can lead to severe thermal spikes, loss of cabin heat, and long-term cylinder head gasket distortions.

repairOptions.longevity: Suitable for isolated valve failure; catch early
If overheating has caused internal damage

problems.h4: Drivetrain Cable Corrosion ("Cablegate") - Why the Toyota RAV4 2.5 PHEV Hybrid System Fails
problems.rootCause: The high-voltage electrical cable carrying power to the rear electric motor is highly susceptible to severe galvanic and environmental corrosion at its undercarriage connector boot. Moisture breaches the wire shielding, triggering a hybrid system malfunction error.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replace full harness - requires dropping rear subframe and fuel tank
Only if internal damage has occurred
repairOptions.longevity: Not required for cable corrosion alone
